inputs.root_cause: Applied the same cross-format comparison technique that closed the equivalent xliff obligation (SAL-XLIFF-OBL-130340BC212989D5, event 247) one tick earlier: read ora's own _Walker (stack_xml.py) directly and found it checked node count and nesting depth but never accumulated or checked attribute count anywhere, despite max_entries already being a configured, caller-facing ResourceLimits field -- the identical class of gap xliff's reader had just been found to have against its ubl sibling.
inputs.obligation_targeted: SAL-ORA-OBL-1C91BEA24163FEE8 (ORA-SEC-001) -- already implemented; evidence strengthened, real bug fixed, no status crossing
inputs.acceptance_evidence: 4 new tests prove: an attribute flood on a nested layer is refused; an attribute flood on the <image> root element is refused; an attribute flood on the top-level <stack> element is refused; a document with attributes within the limit still parses.
inputs.regression_tier: full ora package suite (tests/python/ora) plus 6-format regression

execution_steps: 1. After xliff's attribute/text-limit gap closed at event 247, checked ora's own _Walker class (stack_xml.py) for the same class of gap, since ora's stack.xml reader is a structurally similar bounded-XML-tree walker.

2. Found _Walker.child() checked max_xml_nodes (node count) and max_nesting_depth but never accumulated or checked attribute count anywhere, despite max_entries already being a defined, caller-facing ResourceLimits field used by the ubl and (as of event 247) xliff readers.

3. Confirmed this is a genuine, exploitable gap via direct probing before any fix: parse_stack() with 2000 attributes on a <layer> element sailed straight through even with max_entries=5 explicitly configured.
4. Added attribute counting inside _Walker.child() as the first fix. Re-probed: a nested-element attribute flood (on a <layer>) was now correctly refused.

5. A second probe on the <image> root element's own attributes revealed the fix was INCOMPLETE: the root's attributes are read directly in parse_stack() via _require(root, "w") etc. without ever passing through the walker, so a flood on the root itself still sailed through unrejected.

6. A third probe on the top-level <stack> element (stacks[0]) found the identical problem for a second, distinct reason: parse_stack() calls walker.stack(stacks[0], 0) directly rather than walker.child(stacks[0], 0), so stacks[0]'s own attributes (and even its own node-count entry) never passed through any counting logic either.

7. Refactored the shared node+attribute counting logic out of child() into a new _Walker.count_element() method (counts node + attributes together, checked immediately after each update). Called it explicitly for both root and stacks[0] in parse_stack(), in addition to its continued use inside child() for every descendant reached via the existing recursive dispatch.
8. Re-probed all 4 relevant cases (nested-layer flood, root-image flood, top-level-stack flood, and a normal small valid document) and confirmed correct behavior in every case.
9. Ran the full pre-existing ora suite (316 tests, zero new fixtures) against the fix to look for false positives before writing a single new test -- all 316 passed unchanged.

10. Wrote 4 formal tests in the existing test_obligation_security_baseline.py (extending its established pattern). First draft used 50 attributes per fixture, which produced a 448-byte stack.xml exceeding TINY_LIMITS.max_header_bytes=200, causing the wrong limit (max_header_bytes) to fire first and masking the intended 'cumulative attributes' assertion. Fixed by reducing to 8 attributes per fixture (114 bytes, confirmed under 200 via a direct byte-length check).

11. Ran ruff (clean), the full ora suite (320 passed, was 316, +4), and the full 6-format regression (3440 passed, was 3436, +4; same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) confirming zero cross-format regression.

12. Ran skills-first governance: resolve -> add-python-api (COMPOSE_EXISTING_SKILLS), manifest create --write (sfx-a05f04f20598a798, confirmed as the actually-persisted manifest via ls -t .local/skills-first/manifests/), hand-written receipt YAML, closeout --close -> CLOSE_OK.

13. SAL-ORA-OBL-1C91BEA24163FEE8 was already status=implemented before this tick (ORA-SEC-001 covers the broader security baseline). This tick strengthens its evidence with a real, previously-unnoticed exploitable gap fixed, rather than crossing a status boundary -- no obligation is promoted.
